record.field: SQL: views, window functions, performance, injection
Publish the results of the charity run with SQL, speed up the amounts raised, close a security hole and catch a cheater.

field.name: description
field.p: La Course du Cœur is a 10 km charity run: for each kilometre covered by a runner, their sponsors give money to the association. Three editions, 1 800 runners, thousands of split times: the module has all the data, but the results are missing, the list of the runners is slow, the results kiosk has a security hole… and someone cheated.

div.p: Development challenge: SQL. Complete the module trivia_charity_run: the TODOs of the code are numbered like the missions below, and give the details. To explore the data, open a PostgreSQL console: make psql.
After a change of Python code, update the modules (make update): the SQL view is created again. Then click Check: the tab Checker Report lists what is still missing.
Write the SQL view of the results: the time, the pace and the ranks of each runner who reached the finish.
Compute the amount raised without running one query per runner, and add the missing index on the split times of the runners.
💡 Before a query in raw SQL, the changes still in the cache of the ORM must be sent to the database (flush_model()).
search_by_bib_or_name() is open to SQL injection, and it cannot even find Seán O'Brien. Fix it.
In the last edition, a runner took a shortcut: between km 5 and km 10, their time beats the world record of the 5 km (12 min 35 s). Find them with SQL, then disqualify them, and only them.

ul.li: The disqualified runners are not in the results, and the ranks are computed without them.
A pivot view and a graph view of the results.
